body.heading: Every animal has an address
paragraphs: People live in houses, but animals have homes with special names of their own. Some are built by people, like a horse's stable. Some are built by the animals themselves, like a bird's nest or a rabbit's burrow.
Here are twelve animals and their homes. Learn them in pairs, the way the animals live in them!

body.heading: Farm homes
paragraphs: The dog lives in a kennel. The horse lives in a stable. The cow lives in a shed. The pig lives in a pen. The sheep lives in a barn. The hen lives in a coop.

body.heading: Wild homes
paragraphs: The lion lives in a den. The bird lives in a nest. The bee lives in a hive. The frog lives in a pond. The rabbit lives in a burrow. The ant lives in an anthill.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Cover the home words and quiz each other: 'Where does a bee live?' How many can you get right?
2. A burrow, a den and a nest are all homes animals build themselves. Which one would be coziest to sleep in — and which would you visit for honey?

takeaway: Animal homes have special names: kennel, stable, pen, coop, den, nest, hive, burrow and anthill.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
